As regards this decision, it may serve to illustrate what I was talking about that the HVO was organised along the same lines as a normal government because in this decision, a person is appointed the head of a department and it would be quite natural to expect that the president of the HVO would propose to the Presidency the person to be appointed to such a post but in this case we are talking about the very same person, who held both functions. So from that point of view, this is quite odd.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If I can just before we move too much further ahead, you may have misspoke, sir, and I just want to give you the opportunity to correct it. You said in the first phase, the president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna was at the same time the president of the HVO. But as you've described the first phase, the HVO didn't exist yet. Did you mean to say in the early part of the second phase?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That's what I meant, the first few months of the second phase, after the HVO was established but before the HVO got its president.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And you also said a few moments ago that it was sometime in August 1992 that another man became the president of the HVO. Do you know who that was?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And who was that?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: That was Jadranko Prlic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You -- if I can direct your attention to page 32 and 33 of your report, page 25 in the Croatian version, at the bottom of page 32 of the English version, continuing on over to the top of page 33, I believe it's fair to say that you summarise some of the things that you've said in the last few minutes. And I'll just start with the sentence that says, "Within the framework" at the bottom again of page 32. "Within the framework of these regulations, the HZ HB Presidency, as the 'supreme' leadership of the HZ HB originally held exclusive sovereign power while later on the 'supreme' power was exercised by both the HZ HB Presidency and the President of the HZ HB, either directly or through the HZ HB-HVO and other executive and administrative bodies at the HZ HB-HVO level and at the level of the municipal HVOs. Later on, the HZ HB-HVO gradually took over all executive and administrative functions, and to a certain extent also -- also the legislative function." And I believe you were saying a few moments ago in fact that you found that the HVO over time did take on not only executive power but also the legislative power of Herceg-Bosna; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: As regards the last part, some decisions taken by the HVO are such that in a normal division of government, they would be in the purview of the parliament, but I've already stressed that in other modern democratic states, in a state of war or imminent threat of war, the executive power is given certain tasks, it is either the president of the state or the prime minister or both, they are given certain additional responsibilities or additional powers. This is obviously what happened in the second stage of the development of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, and this is why the Presidency of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna did not meet regularly. It actually met very seldom. So to sum up, I would say that in the second phase, the HVO had a very strong position. It had substantial executive and administrative powers and it even had some legislative powers. But at the same time, the Presidency, and in particular the president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, retained a lot of influence and a very strong position.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In terms of the structure of the HVO government itself, if I could ask you, please, to turn to tab 440, which is Exhibit P 00440, and if you have that, you can confirm, sir, that this is the decree on the organisation, responsibilities of the departments and commissions of the Croatian Defence Council and the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna as adopted on the 15th of May 1992?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And if I can ask you to look at Article 8 for an example, can you confirm that when the HVO government was structured in this way, pursuant to this decree, that one of the -- well, in Article 8 we have all the departments at that Time listed including the Department of Defence. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could I ask you next, please, to go to P -- in your tab, in your binders, it will be 128 but it is Exhibit P 00128.

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes. I found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And if I can just direct your attention to page 1 and 2 of the English version, I assume for these purposes, since it's the beginning of the document it's roughly the same in the Croatian version, perhaps all on page 1 but if not, perhaps page 1 and 2 but at the bottom of page 1 of the English version you'll find this paragraph starting with, "The HVO-HZ HB was founded in May 1992." And I'm not going to take everyone's time to read that entire paragraph but if we skip to the end of that page, it says: "However, in time, the above rights and obligations were expanded to a full legislative function because by a change of the statutory decision, earlier right to pass regulation within its own sphere was expanded." And then it goes on to say in the last sentence of that paragraph: "Since for the passing of the regulations it is necessary to define one's political orientation and views, responsibility for determining policy in all spheres was in effect transferred to a certain extent to the HVO-HZ HB." Can you tell us please how that statement and this is a reports of the HVO government for the time period from its creation, in April 1992, to 31 December 1992, it tells us at the top of the first page, how does that enter into your analysis and what you told us in the last few minutes?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes. What is written here in this HVO report on its work in 1992 formed the basis for the part of my report where I say that to a certain extent, it had a legislative function too. It would be very difficult for me to accept that the legislative function as a whole was now in the hands of the HVO. I have to say now that there was a debate on this issue, when I gave evidence here for the first time seven years ago, and I insisted at that time, as I do now, that both the Presidency and the President of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna retained in the second phase very strong powers. So we cannot overlook what the HVO said here, describing its own legislative function, and its own strong position, but on the other hand, we have to take into account the fact that the Presidency continued to be superior to the HVO and the President of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna played a major role in personnel decisions and the operation of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. And again we will come back to some of those items in a few moments, I hope, but before we do that can I ask you next to go to tab 684 or Exhibit P 00684, on the question as you've described it in the last few minutes of the expansion of the HVO's legislative powers. 684. This makes reference to a decision taken on the 17th of October 1992 and can you look at it, please, and can you confirm to the Judges that when you talk about -- I referred you a moment ago to language in Exhibit P 00128, the report on the work of the HVO, where it talked about -- I'll just quickly quote the language again -- you don't have to turn to it, but it talks about: "Because by a change of the statutory decision, the earlier right to pass regulations within its own sphere was expanded." And if you look at Exhibit P 00684, can you tell the Judges whether it was in part as a result of this decision that the legislative powers of the HVO were expanded?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, we are now dealing with a very important subject because we are talking about responsibilities of parties and as a judge I am not allowed to make any mistakes in this matter. If I understand you correctly, and I will try to summarise, you will tell me if what I'm summarising is adequate: To begin with, we have the Croatian council with a Presidency, we have a vice-president and the general secretary, the president of the Presidency is Mr. Mate Boban. That's what's at the onset. Then we have the creation of the HVO, and at that time, we are going to see on the 8th of April 1992, this is what you stated, we will see the creation of a certain form of government of the HVO, and we saw documents to that effect. We noticed, therefore, that Mate Boban, who at the time was wearing two hats, the hat of the president of the HVO as well as the hat of the president of the Presidency of the HZ HB, whose functions in the HVO were replaced by Mr. Prlic who then becomes the president of the HVO, but Mate Boban remains the President of the HZ HB, and just a few moments ago, you told us that he kept very important powers. So at a certain point in time, to qualify the HZ HB, you stated that he had the ability to give directives and he also had a veto, the power of a veto, so in constitutional terms and when we talk about the way a government functions, is it right to say that the reality of the power was exercised by Mate Boban who was also the head of the army and that Mr. Prlic, who was the President of the HVO and then had various ministers, depended on Mate Boban, even as we see it in the last document that we looked at, they had within the HVO the possibility to take law texts, decrees and, et cetera, but as the last text that we saw tells us within its attribution or his attribution, rather, within his powers, it's on Article 1 of the decision of the 3rd of November 1992. So in a certain way, can we not say that we had a sort of a pyramid with the Presidency of the HZ HB on the top, at the head of which was Mate Boban, and underneath we have the HVO, whose president was Mr. Prlic? Was that the functioning structure of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I must say that I largely agree with that approach. When it comes to the relationship between the parliament and the head of state on the one side and the government on the other side, in the modern democratic states, this is not a classical subordination and subordination relationship in which -- but that the government has a high degree of its only responsibility and independence. To what extent this applied to the HVO or maybe it didn't apply to them in practice, it's very hard to say. I must agree with Mr. Scott. He drew our attention to some elements based on which one may conclude that the HVO also had something that is not usual and customary that goes beyond what the government normally has, and that is that it could issue decisions in order to regulate some general issues. The orders to that effect were issued that would normally be issued by the legislative body rather than the government. With that caveat, I have to agree with what you have offered as a summary of my presentation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Professor, I'm going to have to go back now some minutes to the question that I put to you but you have not yet answered, and that was simply that -- try to remember it as close as I can without going back and reading the transcript -- I directed your attention to Exhibit 684 and asked you, in looking at that exhibit, would that illustrate to you or was that one of the bases on which you -- that supports the conclusion that the legislative powers, for example, that you just mentioned of the HVO were expanded in the fall of 1992?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, before the gentleman answers the question I would ask the gentleman to look at the entire Article 1, especially the last two paragraphs, because I think we need to have the answer in context, so if he could look at the last paragraph, the last two paragraphs, because there is a caveat there which would explain why certain powers, as it be, were delegated under the extraordinary circumstances of the time. Keeping in mind of course that the gentleman did indicate that the Presidency was unable to meet on a regular basis due to the conditions on the ground. So I think we have to look at it in context and I think that's -- so I think the gentleman wishes to be fair. I'm giving him an opportunity to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I put -- first put this question about 15 minutes ago, and with all due respect to the Chamber, if I could put and follow my questions and get answers to my questions, and also before the interventions with all respect of the Chamber and of Mr. Karnavas and others it would be helpful. No one is trying to deceive anyone here. The whole document is in the record. Everyone know what is it says. So I still repeat for the third time, for the third time, sir, my question to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If you look at Exhibit P 00684, can you confirm to us that it was in part at least based on this decision in October -- the 17th of October 1992, by which the legislative powers of the HVO were expanded?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes. My answer would be yes to that. This decision is about four types of documents that were issued by the HVO. I believe that document 2, 3 and 4 are not in dispute because they were typical of the executive power. Only the first document, the decree, is in dispute. From that point of view it is interesting because it allowed the HVO to issue decision of general interest, i.e., decisions that would have normally been passed in any modern state by the parliament, i.e., the representative body, in the case of Herceg-Bosna, it would have been the Presidency of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. The fact is that this decision created the norm for such enlargement of the functions of which I have already said that it can be encountered in the constitutional orders of modern democratic states which envisage that under special conditions or under the threat of war, such solutions that would provide the efficient functioning of the state under conditions when the parliament is unable to convene or it cannot be convened on a regular basis. From that point of view --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm terribly sorry for interrupting you but the intervention by Mr. Karnavas which could have been made during the cross-examination was nevertheless important. When you talked about democratic states, you talk about parliaments and so on and so forth, you know that at the time there was a war, and if I compare it to Bosnia and Herzegovina, the President Izetbegovic had also proclaimed a state of war. So there was a special state, something was going on, there was a state of war and in a state of war it is right to say that the parliament cannot convene and somebody has to take decisions. Now, the text that everybody has on the screen shows us that the ones that can take a decision is the HVO. But if we read the last two paragraphs of the Articles, is the following, and I can of course refer to the way some people were nominated. Now, please tell me, and please correct me if I'm mistaken can we not finally say that the HVO within its functioning could not have decided of everything without having a certain form of control of the HZ HB who, as a last resort, had the responsibility and that at any time Mate Boban was able to intervene, since on the one hand there was a state of war and, on the other hand, the HVO, such as it was created, did not transfer, as I think, I may be mistaken, the powers of Mate Boban and the Presidency of the HZ HB completely on the HVO? What do you think of this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I share your opinion. I believe that this decision allowed the HVO to apply this decree; and in the cases when the Presidency was unable to meet, and there was a lot of such cases, the Presidency did not meet very often during that period of time, so it could also pass decisions on such matters that would have otherwise been in -- within the purview of the Presidency. In other words, this was an additional possibility, or maybe an exception, but this does not mean that the presidents could not have decided on the same issue. As for the particular question about the penultimate paragraph, which refers to the subsequent consent of the Presidency of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, this is also another standard or something that is common in normal constitutional orders, which means that a body issues a decision during the state of war, this decision has to be approved by the body that would normally have been in charge of passing such decision. And what it says at the end, that if there is no such consent then the application of such a decision is discontinued, which is only logical in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So let me ask you the most important question, the paramount question. We sometimes spend lots of hours to summarise something but let me ask you this question: What was, according to you, the leeway of Mr. Prlic with respect to Mr. --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear who else --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In order to be able to answer this question, it is not enough to be familiar with the constitution and legal aspects but you have to be aware of the facts. As far as I'm concerned, the president of the HVO had relative independence in his doings but he was subordinated to the president of the HVO [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There must have been a mistake with relation to the president of the HZ HB; is that right? Line 4, page 63. Mr. Scott seems to agree with me. So, Witness, what is it? You read English.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. [In English] Yes, it's okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's okay?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise. Could you please look at line 24 on page 62. I believe this is very significant. The interpreters did not hear the second name that you mentioned and I believe that it should be entered in the transcript, the second name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed, I was asking about Mr. Prlic's leeway with relation to Mr. Mate Boban. So the missing name was Mate Boban's. Very well. Now things have been clear, I hope. Please proceed, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Before we move forward, I think the answer that the Professor gave in response to the point raised by counsel is not really clear -- or right before that. The issue was raised whether -- excuse me -- I just want to make sure -- the issue was raised whether the second reference in line -- page 63, line 4 should be subordinated to the president of the HVO. Mr. President, you suggested that properly should be the president of the HZ HB; and in -- the witness simply responded: "Yes, it's okay." We don't know what: "Yes, it's okay" means.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Professor, so is it correct to say that what you should have said at the -- on page 4 -- line 4 of line [sic] 63 was: "... was subordinated to the president of the HZ HB"?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes, and I apologies. What you are now saying, Mr. Scott, is correct. I said that he had relative independence but that he was also in the position of subordination, and I meant the president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna when I said that. And I thank you for correcting me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If we can try to move forward and then I'll come back to -- again hopefully come back to a couple of questions that are laying in all this, but if we can proceed in steps. On -- in your report, sir, at page 31 of the English version - and I'm afraid in this instance I may not be able to help with you the Croatian citation, but if you can find at -- it's on page 31 of the English version - you make the statement -- if it helps you it's above -- let me find the footnote reference for you. It's right around footnote 107. If you find footnote 107 in the Croatian version you'll be pretty close to the English reference. Let me know when you have that, please.

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In that paragraph, there is this statement, if you can help me, please. It says: "The HZ H Presidency might order the HZ HB-HVO to bring its enactments into conformity with enactments adopted by the HDZ Presidency." Now, hold that thought, please, and if we could then turn to page 47 of the English version and page in this instance I can tell you it's page 37 of the Croatian version -- let me find my own reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, I need some help myself at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Mr. Scott. If you're mentioning footnote 107, then in Croatian it is page 24.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I meant the -- if the Chamber will just give me a moment to just sort this out. I'm sorry, Your Honour, can I have another moment? I have it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott, I thought you meant the last paragraph of page 47 in the English version, which is an interesting passage.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You're absolutely right, Your Honour. I just -- thank you for that, and I just found that just as you were saying the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: On the bottom of page 47 of the English version, and I think when I got lost is when I was trying to help find the Croatian version, I think it's on page 37 of the Croatian version. But you say there that: "Control" -- in that paragraph it says: "Meanwhile, control over the entire territory was in the hands of the HVO and indirectly the HZ HB Presidency as its superior organ." And By the way, there is no dispute about that. But let me ask this question to you, following up on this language and in the questions that have been put to you by the President. Can you identify for the Judges any instance, any instance, in which the HZ HB Presidency invalidated, vetoed, or annulled any action taken by the HVO?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Lack of foundation, Your Honour. First, the gentleman must be asked whether he looked at all of the legislation, all of the Official Gazettes; and if so, then I believe that he can pose that question. We don't know exactly what he looked at, and so I think it would be unfair. Whether he -- whether it was shown to him or not, I don't know, but I think that's a foundational question that must be answered first.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, with this foundation question seems to be the conclusion drawn by the witness after all the preceding paragraphs, a kind of conclusion. Witness, is this last paragraph, in fact, a conclusion you draw?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. This is a conclusion that I arrived at, and I just supplemented it with the sentence in which I made a mistake, the previous sentence. As far as Mr. Scott's question is concerned, I must say that I have reviewed all the documents that were adopted by the bodies of Herceg-Bosna and that were published in the Official Gazette. I had a copy of each edition in my hands at least once, and I must say that I have not come across a single case in which there would be either a situation or a written material or a preamble to a document that it was passed based on the guide-lines of the Presidency or that there was a subsequent veto. However, this does not have to mean that the officials in question were not in constant contacts. So based on what I know and based on what I could read and study, I believe that it would be fair to say that this was the case of relative independence of the presidents of the HVO and the HVO as a whole and that both were subordinated to the presidents -- president of the H -- Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. What was the factual situation like? It is very hard for me to tell based on the written materials.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm going to come back because you give long answers, and I wanted to ask you this very specifically. First we are talking about the de jure situation, and I think you've made it clear this afternoon -- and in fact again let me just make it clear to the courtroom, there is no dispute about that. De jure, the president -- the HZ HB Presidency could invalidate or direct the actions of the HVO government; that's de jure. Now, again, answer this specific question, this specific question only, please. In your research, did you come across any instance in which the HZ HB Presidency invalidated, vetoed, or annulled an action by the HVO government?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: The answer to your first question is yes, de jure; and de facto, I don't know of any such decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Before we move on, then, in terms of some of the aspects of governmental power in your report, could I ask you to look at tab 306, which is P 00306?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you. If you can look at that for a moment, and this just falls under the -- kind of gotten away from this a bit, but we were talking about the features of statehood and the powers of the government. And do you see, for example, in Exhibit P 00306 that there was a decree on public enterprises in the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna which could set up a number of administrative bodies, for example, production, transmission, supply of electricity, water management, the telephone service, et cetera? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And there is a reference in Article 1, item H, to the Official Gazette of the HZ HB. Was that Official Gazette known as the Narodni List?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And what role did the Narodni List play in the governmental structure or legal structure of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: The Narodni List published all decisions passed by the bodies of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. That was the Official Gazette, such as the states have in order to publish their laws and other regulations. One should also mention that in the former state, within the republics of the former Yugoslavia, even the municipalities published their own regulations in the Official Gazettes, but not a gazette that was their own but, rather, in the Official Gazette of the republic that they belonged to.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Can I then move on to -- if you can turn to page 24 of your report in the English version or page -- excuse me, Croatian page 9, doesn't seem to be right to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Again, please, if the courtroom will just give me a moment, it's in reference to paragraph -- footnote 76.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If you can find in the Croatian version, Professor, your footnote 76. I'm sure it's my mistake for having written down the wrong page or something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: It's 19.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I dropped the one, obviously, it said nine instead of 19. Thank you, Judge Trechsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If you can look at page 19 of the Croatian version, sir, and in reference to footnote 76, if -- that will make the citation very specific you make this statement: "The HVO exercises centralised control over the work of municipal HVOs and has the power to annul and abolish their enactments and dissolve municipal HVOs." Can you comment further on that and indicate how that fits into your assessment of the governmental powers of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes. I think this is an important power that the HVO has, and as I say in this part of my analysis, this establishes an effective state government or governance in the entire territory of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. Regardless of the number of instances in which this kind of control is exerted by the HVO over the municipalities, it is certain that this kind of power is quite important, and the other party is in a subordinate position to an organ that may exercise this kind of power and right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, following directly from what was said, and more specifically from this passage on this decree published in the Narodni List, you studied all the texts, and as you know, there is a decision establishing the Croatian Council of Herceg-Bosna of the 18th of November, 1991, which we find in Exhibit 78. Article 7, this is the one that keeps being referred to in all the HVO decrees. If you read Article 7, you see that the legislative organ of the HZ HB is the Presidency; in theory, it is the Presidency. When the HVO is created, according to you - because you are the constitutional expert - is there no delegation of the legislative powers to the HVO presided over by Mr. Prlic whilst remaining under the control of the Presidency, under the control of the HZ HB?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is my conviction that what happened is that the -- all the powers pertaining to the executive and administrative power were delegated to the HVO and in exceptional circumstances the HVO could take decisions that were within the purview of the legislative power which was not delegated in its totality from the Presidency to the HVO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] However, such transfer or devolution as you qualified it, constitutionally speaking, as it were, should it not have been sort of endorsed by all the 30 municipalities that were part of the Croatian council?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, from the standpoint constitutional law the Presidency was the body that represented the municipalities. This was how things were set up, and in this manner, the municipalities were represented through its representatives, through their representatives in the Presidency, when any decisions regarding the HVO were taken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, you're not really answering my question. You say that in your view, there was a transfer of power from the Presidency to the HVO level. And my question, my technical question, is this: Such transfer, should it not have been approved of, endorsed, by all of the municipalities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, as far as I'm concerned, the controversial thing when the Presidency was set up was the fact that it was set up on a single-party and single-ethnicity basis but what is not controversial --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry, I'm not speaking about the ethnic level. I'm speaking about a purely legal level. Legally speaking, there are municipalities that create the Croatian council of Herceg-Bosna with a Presidency. Then, Mr. Mate Boban was the President of the Presidency. And the constitutional text, Article 7, states that the legislative power rests with the Presidency. When the HVO was created, with various ministries or departments and Mr. Prlic became the president of the HVO, if there was indeed the transfer that you mentioned, did this de jure transfer have to be approved or not by the municipalities? But if there was no such transfer, does that not mean that the legislative power is deferred but it is done whilst being controlled by the HZ HB, and that therefore, there is no need to have the approval of it by all of the municipalities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, one could take a very strict view that I actually mention in my analysis, and that is that some of the decisions are of a constitutional-legal nature. In other words, that if we have a meeting where the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna was established, this is not something that should be changed by the Presidency but a similar meeting involving the representatives of all the municipalities that comprise the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna should be organised. I personally take the view that this transfer of some elements of the legislative powers in the conditions of war is not something that is as significant as the establishment of the President, of the function of the President of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna which was also not done in accordance with the procedure whereby all the municipalities could give their approval. So there were decisions that were even more momentous that were taken by the Presidency as some kind of a regular legislative body.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Mr. Scott? I know my questions are lengthy but they are relevant ones, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Of course they are, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If I could just follow up, sir, in reference to the President's questions, in fact, to Exhibit -- if we can go back I'm afraid to Exhibit P 00684, in terms of the delegation of legislative power to the HVO. Do you still have 684, there, sir?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: [In English] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If you look at the opening language of that document, does it say, "Pursuant to the decision of the establishment of the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna, Article 7" - as the President just referred to - "the Presidency of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna at its session of 17 October 1992, adopted the decision." So did not the Presidency of the HZ HB, by its decision made in its session on the 17th of October 1992, delegate these legislative powers to the HVO?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: I'm afraid that I didn't really understand your question. I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Let's try again. If you look at the top of Exhibit 684, which says: "Pursuant to the decision on the establishment of the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna, Article 7, the Presidency of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna" - and look at this language, please - "at its session of 17 October 1992 adopted the decision." So, sir, cannot the Judges understand that this indeed is the decision by which the legislative -- by which the Presidency of Herceg-Bosna delegated the legislative power to the HVO?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes. I agree that this decision, inasmuch as it pertains to the regulations about the organisation and some issues of general interest, and the situations that have to be dealt with on an emergency basis, mean that the powers of the HVO have been extended, the HVO is given a legal foundation to take certain decisions that would be in the purview of the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If I can just perhaps close this part of the questions by reference back to something we looked at much earlier this afternoon now, if I can direct you, sir, back to paragraph -- excuse me, page 32 of your report, and if you want to find it, it follows footnote 108 in the Croatian version. It's on page 25 in the Croatian version.

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, let's go back to where we started at least in part some -- an hour or so ago, perhaps two hours ago now, and I just direct you back to your own words on the bottom of page 32 in the English version, where you say: "Later on, the HZ HB-HVO gradually took over all executive, administrative functions and to a certain extent also the legislative function." Isn't that in fact borne out by everything we looked at and discussed in the last few hours?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I suggest that might be a good time for the recess.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's look at the time you've used so far and we shall resume around 6.00. You'll then have an hour left. And you would then by the end of the day have used the three hours. It would be nice if you could finish by 7.00. Let's have a break. We shall resume around 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott, we have some difficulties connected with the court reporter. He can't work later than 7.10 so you have to stop at ten to 7.00. Everybody will leave the courtroom, but for Mr. Ibrisimovic and his co-counsel, and we shall continue until 10 past 7.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Especially under those circumstances I'm not sure I can finish tonight but I'll certainly move as quickly as I reasonably can. I believe the time record indicates that so far I've used one hour and 23 minutes, or in other words less than half of my allocated time, but having said that I'm still going to move as quickly as I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, if we can just -- I'd like to just direct your attention to various documents and you may be jumping from document to document a bit but as you just heard me say I would like to try to move us along as quickly as reasonably possible. When you were considering the next topic, you talk about the direct subordination of Herceg-Bosna to international law which again you touched on much earlier this afternoon. And you discuss at some length at pages 48 and 49 of your report some of the reasons for the creation of the HZ HB. I'll have to leave that part of your report to speak for itself. Let me ask you please to turn to Exhibit P 00424 which you will find in your binders at tab 424, please.

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: This is the decree on transferring the resources of the JNA and something called the SSNO to the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, to the ownership of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. Can you just briefly describe to the Judges how this -- how the citation to this document refer -- links to your conclusions about the Herceg-Bosna or the HVO government in fact having the characteristics of government or a state?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: I mentioned this decree in my analysis because it shows that the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna made sovereign and independent decisions regarding the powers that it had and regardless of the powers that the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina had. It can be seen when the assets of the JNA are transferred and no mention is made to any transfer of such assets to any bodies of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina but only to the organs of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right, sir, I would like to next direct your attention to the establishment of the military prosecutor's offices and if I can ask you please to go to Exhibit P 00590 or tab 590 in your binder, please.

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And again, let me just ask you can you comment on the relevance of this document, that is on the establishment the district military prosecutor's offices in reference to, again, the characteristics of statehood of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: In the sphere of the legislative power, there was a difference in the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. By that I mean to say that it did not set up its own Supreme Court but it set up a department of the Supreme Court of Bosnia-Herzegovina, but regardless of all that, the documents produced by the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna clearly show that full legislative power was assumed by this community. This can be seen from the fact that it is establishing new organs, new bodies, such as the district military prosecutor's offices, as seen here, it can be seen in the sphere of human resources or personnel because the organs of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna decide who will be appointed to various offices in the judiciary, in the courts and in the prosecutor's offices. It showed that the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna and its organs carried out legislative functions and this includes the HVO. They were independent bodies and independent government independent from Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: We've talked mostly today about what we might call the executive and legislative powers but would you agree, sir, that another badge, if you will, of statehood is the establishment of a judicial branch, with prosecutors, judges, courts, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: That's correct. Any effective state government has to have all those functions and all those bodies, executive, legislative and judiciary.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I would like to now turn to the topic, please, of the reaction of the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina and to the constitutional court of Bosnia-Herzegovina to the establishment of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna and if I can direct your attention, please, to page 10 of the report, English page 10, or Croatian page 8.

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In that -- on that page, you make reference to the fact that an opinion of the Ministry of Justice and Administration of Bosnia-Herzegovina issued an opinion on the 20th of November 1991. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you just quickly summarise for us the opinion expressed by the Ministry of Justice and Administration on the 20th of November 1991?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise but if the Prosecutor refers to page 8 in the B/C/S and page 10 in the English version, then there is no reference in this text to the decision of the-- opinion of the ministry but it says here that the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina, pursuant to an opinion of the ministry, it was actually an opinion that was made by the government on the basis of the opinion of the ministry. I am sure that Professor Ribicic will agree with me that this is how he actually phrased it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm not sure of the nature of the objection or clarification but we are indeed talking about the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell us about the opinion -- the -- what you address on the middle of page 10 of the English version of your report and page 8 of the Croatian version, the paragraph that begins with the words, "Much earlier"?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes. The source that I quote here, this was published in Oslobodjenje daily paper, it is quite clear that the Ministry of Justice and Administration issued an opinion and then the government on the basis of that opinion concluded, reached the conclusion, that the decisions of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna are illegal and illegitimate and contrary to the constitution. So what it says here, that this is contrary to the interests of the state of BH and all its citizens and nations, this is the conclusion of the government that is based on the opinion of the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can we just confirm for the record, sir, that if this opinion was issued on the 20th of November 1991, that was just two days after Herceg-Bosna declared its existence on the 18th of November 1991, so that the reaction of the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina was basically immediate; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In that opinion, it refers to, at least as summarised here, and in fact it's in footnote 30 of your report, that the suggestion was that proceedings be initiated before the Constitutional Court. Do you see that in footnote 30?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And are you aware, sir, that in fact, proceedings were initiated before the Constitutional Court of Bosnia-Herzegovina on this question? Sir, my question --

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Just a moment. Yes. The statement of reasons appended to the decision of the constitutional court, it is clear that the government had filed this request before the constitutional court.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can I ask you, please, to turn to tab 346 which should be Exhibit P 00346?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you just tell us what that is, please?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: This is a letter in response to the request. It is a letter written by the Secretary-General of the Croatian Democratic Union of Bosnia-Herzegovina, in response to a previous memo from the constitutional court, providing an explanation that the Croatian Democratic Union has done everything to create a new state --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you just assist the Judges, please, the letter from Mr. Markesic is addressed to someone named Mr. Dautbasic. Can you tell the Judges please who Mr. Dautbasic was as of July 1992?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Dautbasic was the president of the constitutional court of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina so this was a letter from the secretary-general of the Croatian Democratic Union of Bosnia and Herzegovina to the president of the constitutional court.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can I ask to you turn next, please, in your binder, to 421? Which is Exhibit P 00421.

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Once again, can you tell the Judges, just briefly tell the Judges what this document is and how it fits into the constitutional court litigation?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: This is a letter or a memo from the president of the constitutional court to the Croatian Democratic Union, regarding the proceedings to evaluate the constitutionality and legality of the decision on the establishment and some other decisions of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. In this letter, a request is made for those documents that are the subject of the request of the government of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina regarding the evaluation of the constitutionality and legality to be submitted to the Court. In this letter the president of the constitutional court complains that they are asking for those documents for the second time now, yet they have not received any yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Then could I next ask to you go to in your divider, tab 476, which is Exhibit P 00476? And can you tell the Judges, I believe the Judges may have seen this document before, but can you tell the Judges what that document is, then?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: This is the decision of the constitutional court of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, annulling the decision on the establishment of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, and eight other decisions and decrees taken by the Presidency of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. This decision annuls, on the basis of their unconstitutionality, some other acts of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Can you assist us, Professor, if you look at the top of that document, it makes reference to the Official Gazette of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Now, we've talked earlier today about the Official Gazette of Herceg-Bosna being the Narodni List. Do you know what the Official Gazette of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, how that was referred to or described during this time? That is if one were to say Narodni List for Herceg-Bosna how would you describe the Official Gazette for Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Sluzbeni List is the Official Gazette of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. This is where the organs of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina must publish all their decisions and those decisions cannot enter into force before they are published there. The Narodni List played a similar role in the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And with reference to the Official Gazette of Bosnia-Herzegovina, can we see on the top of this document that this is a reference that it was published in volume number 16 at page 450 on the 18th of September 1992? That is that the decision of the constitutional court was published in the Official Gazette?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And, sir, I'm not going to take the time to show it to you because I believe it's already been admitted into evidence but -- as Exhibit P 08060, issued on the 20th of January 1994, but did you ever become aware that the same constitutional court also declared the Croatian republic, not the community, but the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna unconstitutional or illegal?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: [In English] Just a moment, please. [Interpretation] Yes. At a later stage, the constitutional court issued a decision annulling the proclamation of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna. In this decision, the constitutional court of Bosnia-Herzegovina invokes this decision, annulling the decision on the establishment of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna and the constitutional court also stresses that an unconstitutional entity such as the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna is now being replaced or being transformed into another entity which is even more unconstitutional because it assumes even greater powers wresting them away from the hands of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you for that. If we can move on to another part of the report which deals with the relationship between the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna and the Republic of Croatia, and again we have to understand that the Judges have both your report and your testimony in the Kordic case, so let me just ask you about a couple of specific exhibits. Can I ask you, please, to turn to number 735 in your binder which is Exhibit P 00735? Let me know when you have that, please.

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes, I found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you just tell us what that is and again relate it to the observations made in your report?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: This is a decision to import goods from the Republic of Croatia. There is a special regulation about the status of the goods that arrived in Herceg-Bosna from the Republic of Croatia. What is interesting here is the fact that this issue had been discussed at a meeting of the leaderships of the HDZ's of Croatia and Herceg-Bosna on the 27th of December 1991. In addition to this issue, several others were mentioned. For example, the customs, the transit of goods crossing the border, the issue of Croatian money and so on. I first analysed what I found in the Official Gazette and only later did I find out about the meeting that I've just mentioned. As I was reading this, and some other decision, it seemed to me that this was an attempt to come up with an integral decision for all the issues that were still pending within the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, and then from the transcript of the meeting, I realised that this was the same -- these were the same issues that were raised by President late Franjo Tudjman during this meeting that I have mentioned. This means that I could arrive at the conclusion that some of the documents that were passed by the bodies of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna had been previously agreed at the political level within the Croatian Democratic Union and not only in Bosnia and Herzegovina but also with the officials of that same party in Croatia. Based on that, I concluded that some of the decisions were passed by the bodies of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna were of such a nature that either their -- they were the result of the agreements reached outside that entity or served to cover the true nature of the relationship between the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna and the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If I can just direct your attention very quickly to the end of Article 2, is it correct that the effect of this decision, among other things, was to exempt goods imported from Croatia from any sort of customs duty or tax that would otherwise apply to imported goods?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: That's correct. Those goods enjoyed privileged status in comparison with some other goods that arrived from other states.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And if we can go then to Article 5 and can you just tell us please because you mention this in this a number of places in your report, the role played, what you found in your research about the use of the Croatian dinar as the currency in Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Excuse me for this minor intervention, my colleague informs me that in the previous answer, the gentleman said "borders" and not "states." "Arriving from other borders." Here it states in English, it's line 23, comparison with other page, page 83, "comparison with some other goods that arrived from other states." Perhaps he could -- is this a mistake, borders? This is how it was in Croatian, I don't know how it was translated but this is what I was told. I apologise for the intervention.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Professor, if you've heard counsel's comments if you could clarify that further?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I can agree with this clarification. Here we are talking about the same border but the goods were different, and the goods arriving from Croatia were in -- enjoyed privileged status with regard to other.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. If we could go, please, because our time is short, to the use of the Croatian dinar, can you tell the Judges what you found in that respect and one particular example is in Article 5 of this same document.

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes. In the documents issued by the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, it was insisted on the use of Croatian dinars, so some of the documents were changed only to incorporate that. The Croatian dinar as the legal tender. That was the only reason to change some documents. They were redrafted because Croatian dinars had to be incorporated in them. At the aforementioned meeting of the HDZ leadership on the 27th December 1991, there was a debate about the population of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna were in a bad or negative economic position because of the unauthorised printing of the Yugoslav dinar in Belgrade. So there was a discussion to the effect whether this should be solved by establishing a special tender of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina or perhaps this should be resolved in a different way, and this different way can be seen in this decision, i.e., the Croatian dinar was adopted as the legal tender and that's why the regulations of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna had to be redrafted.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can I please just as one more example on this point ask you to look at Exhibit P 00447, at tab 447 of your binder, please?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can you just confirm to us, sir, that again this is just a decree issued around the 22nd of September 1992 actually by the HVO which we have been talking about today, this is not issued by the Presidency, this is issued by the HVO over the name of Jadranko Prlic on the regulation of payment transactions and the use of Croatian dinars; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's correct. Pursuant to this provision, the payment transactions in Herceg-Bosna were in Croatian dinars, and there are some other provisions which guarantee the implementation, i.e., envisage consequences for the lack or the failure to implement this decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And sir I think one final document, if I can ask you to go to 7825? Exhibit P 07825? Do you have it?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: [In English] No, I could not find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Maybe it's -- 7825? No?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: 78 -- now I have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you. This is a declaration issued by the -- apparently issued by the Chamber of Deputies, that's the way it's described in the English translation as the Chamber of Deputies of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna dated the 8th of February 1994. Can you just briefly describe to the Judges any role that this document played in your analysis, and if I could ask you in particular to direct your attention to Roman numeral II at paragraph number 2?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: This is a declaration which was primarily intended for the purpose of creating as good as possible conditions for the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna to be able to become a republic in the future federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina. As a result of that, there were major changes, i.e., transformation of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna into the Croatian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and this declaration and particularly -- puts a particular emphasis on what the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna advocated in a situation when it became clear that the hostilities and the war would stop and that a new state organisation would be put in place.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Professor, I can't -- I can't resist directing your attention to Roman numeral VII on page 4 of the English version, but in any event Roman numeral VII, you see where the House of Deputies says, "We salute the founding and the work of the tribunal for war crimes in the former Yugoslavia. We have no doubts as to its impartiality and we hope it will be prepared to condemn all crimes and do so efficaciously." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In conclusion, Professor, of the direct examination, you published essentially this expert report in a book that is titled, "Genesis of a delusion." And I just wonder if you could tell us the reason and the thinking behind that title of the book? Why did you call -- when you took this report and essentially published, why did you give it the title, "Genesis of a delusion?"?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: The title was suggested to me by the publisher. The title page is also their creation. I'm talking about three publishers actually, one from Sarajevo, one from Zagreb and one from Idrija in Slovenia. What I wanted to say by this book has been said in the preface to the book entitled, "So that it may not repeat in the future." So the main motive of my book was to draw attention to the mistakes that --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I apologise for interrupting you. Our time is short and I'm doing everything I can to accommodate everyone, including the Chamber, the court reporter, the Defence, so we can finish today and they can have as much time tomorrow as possible. First, let me stay on my existing question. You've said that the name was suggested to you, the name "Genesis of a Delusion," but I assume that it wasn't -- that name wasn't imposed on you and you agreed to that title and my question to you, sir, is what is the meaning of "Genesis of a Delusion"? What delusion, delusion by who, who was deluded? Tell us what you meant by that.

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: Yes. I obviously agreed to the title. But there is an attempt for this title to be somewhat striking, in order to encourage sales. But I agreed to the title.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: That's what publishers do. We understand that. But, sir, again, what delusion, please?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: This is what I explained seven years ago, what I've tried to explain today when I told you two stories about Herceg-Bosna. One story is from the Official Gazette and the other story is what we can find in the testimonies of the actors or records of the meetings that was published at the end of the book, which shows what the real relationship was between the Republic of Croatia and the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. This particularly refers, at least in my view, to the part at the meeting which speaks about the representatives of the Croatian HDZ saying one thing and doing another thing. They said that they were in favour of the independent Bosnia-Herzegovina and what they did, they were working towards merging the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna to the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, having clarified that, I want to come back and give the opportunity to answer the question you started to answer, and that is, I believe you said something along the lines of can you tell the Judges in closing, perhaps this is the last question, what made you decide to publish this book? What was your motivation in doing that?

utterances.speaker: CIRIL RIBICIC
utterances.text: My motivation, as I've already said it, and as the title of the preface says, is -- was to draw attention to the mistakes and shortcomings that accompanied the establishment of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna and the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna, that shouldn't be repeated by those who may find themselves in the similar situation in the future, when they try to establish a new state or quasi-state community.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Professor Ribicic, first of all I want to apologise if I've hurried you and been -- rushed you a bit. I apologise for that, no offence was intended but we are trying to accommodate everyone as much as possible. I want to thank you for coming to The Hague again, some seven years later than the first time or so and giving your testimony. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: That concludes direct examination, Your Honour, I hope the Chamber will appreciate the fact that I did everything possible to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Scott. And I would like to congratulate you for really doing your best to shorten the examination-in-chief because you put the most appropriate question to this witness. Thank you for that. Witness, you will now leave this courtroom in a couple of seconds. You will no longer meet the Prosecutor in the meantime. You will come back tomorrow. You are now a court witness and as you know, we will reconvene tomorrow at 2.15 p.m.. You will therefore come back. I will now retire with my colleague. I will also like everybody to leave the courtroom briefly. I would like to ask Mr. Ibrisimovic and his team to stay because at 1900 hours, 7.00 p.m., so I would like to invite everybody to come back tomorrow at 2.15 p.m., thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 11th day of December, 2007, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.49 p.m.,
